question: Why is B3 (10M-row atomic L2 corpus, RP-4G) at ~210s vs the 120s target, and can a parse/rounding fast path in native/runner close it?

fast_path_experiment.change: Allocation-free decimal rounding + field-scanning JSON parse (fallback to serde Value path) replacing serde_json::from_str + Decimal::parse in parse_event_line. Uncommitted working-tree state at session start; evaluated then REVERTED (git clean for native/runner/src/main.rs).

differential_equal.note: Reports identical modulo elapsed_ms and RSS sampling fields.

fast_path_experiment.conclusion: No measurable speedup and no memory benefit. Parse+rounding is a negligible share of B3 runtime.

chunk_sweep_b3_slice_1_97M_head_binary.conclusion: Per-batch flush (engine.add_data + engine.run + clear_data) overhead is not the bottleneck; larger chunks are slightly worse. The 8MB chunk of the B3 harness is already near-optimal.

findings.root_cause: B3 is bound by nautilus BacktestEngine per-event dispatch (add_data/run through cache, clock, actors and portfolio) at ~57k events/s on this VM, not by NDJSON parsing, decimal conversion, report emission (B3 reports are 637KB), or batching. Speeding up parse/rounding cannot yield the required >=1.74x.
options_not_pursued_this_cycle: Profile nautilus internals (cargo flamegraph / perf) and reduce per-event engine cost; changes the certified replay path and needs full differential re-validation (F-fixtures, accounting, conformance).
Feed the engine only strategy-consumed data per event (semantic change to the native path; needs new conformance proof).
Run B3 corpus replay out-of-process in parallel shards (violates the single-tape causal order of the corpus; not a valid B3 measurement).
findings.resource_note: All measurements on this VM with the soak test running; only one bench-class job at a time.
